overview: Global tensions and domestic political milestones headline today's news alongside notable commercial real estate financing transactions and regional developments. In the commercial real estate sector, major lenders are backing significant retail portfolio acquisitions and multi-family construction conversions. San Francisco voters are evaluating critical local policy directions and political campaigns. Meanwhile, Hawaii stories highlight council debates over short-term rentals and community infrastructure challenges.

items.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
items.summary: A Russian bombing attack killed 26 people at a southern Ukrainian village aid center, according to local officials.

items.title: US midterms campaign 'shattering' spending records to be most expensive ever
items.summary: The 2026 US midterms campaign is on track to be the most expensive ever, projected to cost nearly $12 billion.

items.title: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
items.summary: Millions of Americans turning to AI chatbots for election information face misleading answers and unauthorized candidate recommendations.

items.title: Northwind Provides $231M Construction Loan to Convert 675 Third Avenue
items.summary: David Werner Real Estate Investments and Metroloft secured a $231 million construction loan to convert a Midtown Manhattan office into multifamily residential.

items.title: Nuveen Acquires $445M Retail Portfolio Across Three Western States
items.summary: Nuveen Real Estate acquired a 13-property retail portfolio across California, Colorado, and Washington for $445.5 million.

items.title: Final push: Scott Wiener defends lead as field army knocks on 311,000th door
items.summary: Scott Wiener's congressional campaign and an allied super PAC executed one of San Francisco's largest canvassing operations.

items.title: The U.S. midterms could be a big swing left. San Francisco is poised to double down on its gilded age.
items.summary: San Francisco voters appear poised to approve a suite of policy measures reflecting the city's wealthy donor class priorities.

items.title: We asked every S.F. politician and major candidate: How would you fix housing affordability?
items.summary: San Francisco politicians and major candidates shared their specific proposed plans for addressing local housing affordability.

items.title: Hilo tsunami museum is ‘back full-time’ after financial woes
items.summary: The Pacific Tsunami Museum in downtown Hilo has reopened seven days a week with paid staff following past financial struggles.

items.title: A 6-Month Vacation? Hawaiʻi Council Deadlocked On Short-Term Rental Bill
items.summary: A Hawaii council deadlocked on a short-term rental bill that would expand vacation rental zones and lengthen the short-term threshold to 180 days.

items.title: She’s Famous As The Shark Whisperer. These Divers Recall A Toxic Boss
items.summary: More than a dozen former workers reported workplace abuses at One Ocean Diving, which operates cageless shark tours on the North Shore.

wiki.title: Sovetsky Soyuz-class battleship
wiki.extract: The Sovetsky Soyuz-class battleships were a class of battleships begun by the Soviet Union in the late 1930s but never brought into service.
